newsitem.title: INDIA: India says offered quicker trade curb phase-out.
newsitem.headline: India says offered quicker trade curb phase-out.

text.p: India said on Thursday that it had signalled its willingness to speed up the proposed elimination of import restrictions at inconclusive talks this week in Geneva.

The Commerce Ministry said in a statement that India's major trading partners, which had objected to New Delhi's initial proposal to phase out curbs over nine years, had also shown some flexibility in the two days of talks ended on Wednesday.
The talks under the auspices of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) were suspended on Wednesday until June 30 to give all participants "a period of reflection".
"A determined effort was made to reach an understanding on the period for withdrawal of quantitative restrictions," the statement said.
"In this process, India signalled its willingness to consider a reduced phase-out period. In response, India's major trading partners indicated certain amount of flexibility on their part."

The ministry said that the deliberations within the WTO Committee on Balance of Payments Restrictions remained inconclusive on the "central issue of a phase-out period acceptable to the entire membership".
Indian Commerce Secretary P.P. Prabhu told the committee that the nine-year phase-out period was needed to avoid "any precipitate decline in our reserves triggering a balance of payments crisis".
India's plan would remove quantitative restrictions such as quotas dating back 40 years on imports ranging from automobiles and agricultural produce to toilet soap and clothing.

The statement said Prabhu noted that "the components of the balance of payments indicate a degree of potential volatility, with heavy reliance on inward remittances from Indians residing abroad, NRI (non-resident Indians') deposits and portfolio investment".
Prabhu referred to a decline in the rate of export growth, increased dependence on imported crude and "the burgeoning oil imort costs, and external debt burden".
The statement said the minister asked the WTO committee to accept India's proposal to phase out the restrictions in three phases of three years each.

But it noted that some delegations felt that India's foreign exchange reserves were such that quantitative restrictions were no longer justified, and these countries pushed for a transitional period of two to three years.
Among the countries pressing India to end the curbs are the United States, the European Union, Japan, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
